input_notes.requirement_id_source: Identifiers S1-S13 are taken exactly as given in the functional requirements port.
input_notes.priority_field: Each requirement carries a numeric 'priority' (1.0-6.0). The input does not state whether a lower number means higher priority; it is reported as given and not interpreted.
input_notes.explicit_vs_inferred: 'requirement_description' is copied verbatim from the input. 'implicit_behaviors' are inferences that are necessary to fulfil the stated requirement and are labelled '(inferred)'. 'ambiguities' list information that is missing or unclear in the input.

global_ambiguities: The project description refers to a city-wide service run by the city administration ('CityBike'), while the system name is 'campus-bike' and one constraint refers to 'the location of the university'. Whether the scope is a city or a university campus is unclear.

The project description requires compliance with 'EU or China standards, depending on the location of the university'; the deployment jurisdiction(s) is not stated, so the applicable regulatory set is undetermined.
No requirement describes how a rental ends (returning/locking the bike, where bikes may be returned, how return is detected), although S7, S9, S10 and S12 depend on the rental lifecycle ending.

No pricing / tariff model is given (pay-per-use is mentioned in the project description; S9 mentions additional overtime charges; S10 mentions minute/day/week rentals), so how fees are calculated is unspecified.

The physical bike-side capability (how a bike is unlocked after QR / four-digit code registration, and how bike location is obtained) is not described; the project description states bikes' locations must be tracked and unlocked using a QR code.
The meaning of the numeric 'priority' attribute (ascending or descending importance) is not defined.
project_constraints_explicit: Comply with GDPR and the Privacy Directive.
Comply with relevant security and data protection standards such as ISO 27001.
Designed to minimize carbon footprint and promote sustainable mobility.
User-friendly and easy to use for all potential riders.
Ensure security and privacy of user data, including payment information.
Compatible with a variety of third-party payment platforms.
Track and display the location of available bikes within a 1000-meter radius and unlock them using a QR code.
Accessible through both web and mobile devices.
Comply with local regulations and standards, including EU or China standards, depending on the location of the university.
The design can rely on: container orchestration platform, service registry and discovery, API gateway, message broker, and distributed tracing (stated as permitted, not mandated).

requirements.requirement_description: The biker must be able to register with the app by providing their name, email address, phone number, and selecting a password, and provide Zip code of residential address (optional information). The app must ensure that user information is secured with an end-to-end encryption of information between user device and app database.
implicit_behaviors: (inferred) The system must persist a biker account record containing name, email, phone number, password credential and optional zip code.
(inferred) Registration input must be validated (e.g. required fields present) before an account is created.
(inferred) Personal data is collected, so the GDPR / Privacy Directive constraints of the project description apply to this data.
(inferred) Registration triggers the verification step described in S2.
ambiguities: 'End-to-end encryption of information between user device and app database' is not precisely defined: it is unclear whether it means protection in transit only, in transit and at rest, or that data remains encrypted such that intermediate application layers cannot read it.
Uniqueness rules for an account (e.g. whether email and/or phone number must be unique) are not stated.
Password policy (strength, rules) is not stated.
Whether registration is available on both web and mobile (project description requires both channels) or only in the mobile app is not stated.

requirements.requirement_description: The app must sent a verification code via an SMS or email that is valid for 30 minutes. If the code is not entered within 30 seconds it is expired.
implicit_behaviors: (inferred) The system must generate a verification code, deliver it through an SMS or email channel, and record its issue time to evaluate expiry.
(inferred) The account is not considered verified until a valid code is entered.
(inferred) Delivery of SMS or email implies interaction with an external messaging capability.
ambiguities: The validity period is internally inconsistent: 'valid for 30 minutes' versus 'if the code is not entered within 30 seconds it is expired'.
It is not stated whether verification applies only at registration or also at other moments (e.g. login, password reset).
Who chooses between SMS and email (biker or system), and whether both contacts must be verified, is not stated.
Behaviour after expiry (re-sending a code, retry limits) is not stated.

requirements.requirement_description: The biker must be able to login to the app via their email and password or by using their biometric thumb-impression. The login module must flush out user thumb impression as soon as the user has been able to login.
implicit_behaviors: (inferred) The system must authenticate a biker against stored credentials and establish a session.
(inferred) Biometric login requires a device capable of capturing fingerprints, which is typically only available on mobile devices, not all web clients.
(inferred) Fingerprint data is biometric personal data and falls under the GDPR constraint of the project description.
ambiguities: It is unclear whether the thumb impression is matched on the device or transmitted to and matched by the system; 'flush out' could refer to device memory or server-side storage.
How biometric login is enrolled/linked to an account is not described.
Failed-login handling (lockout, retries) is not stated.
Whether biometric login must be offered on the web channel is not stated.

requirements.requirement_description: Biker must be logged out of the app by clicking on logout button or after an inactivity of 15 minutes to avoid unnecessary (idle) users on the app in a session.
implicit_behaviors: (inferred) The system must track last activity per session and terminate sessions after 15 minutes of inactivity.
(inferred) An explicit logout action must terminate the session.
ambiguities: 'Inactivity' is not defined (no user interaction in the app vs. no request to the system); a biker riding a bike for 90 minutes (S6) will likely be inactive in the app.
Whether an automatic logout affects an ongoing rental or the delivery of expiry notifications (S9) is not stated.

requirements.requirement_description: Biker can view all of available bikes in close proximity defined by him/her such as specifying that they only want to see bikes that are available in a proximity of 100 meters.
implicit_behaviors: (inferred) The system must know the current location of the biker and the current location and availability status of each bike.
(inferred) The system must filter available bikes by a biker-defined distance from the biker's location.
(inferred) The biker's location is personal data subject to the GDPR constraint.
ambiguities: The project description states bikes are displayed 'within a 1000-meter radius'; it is unclear whether 1000 m is the maximum, a default, or a fixed radius, relative to the biker-defined proximity in S5.
How fresh the displayed bike location/availability must be is not stated.
Whether bikes are presented as a map, list, or both is not stated.

requirements.requirement_description: App must help the biker to navigate to the available bike that they have selected. Upon reaching bike, biker should scan the code on bike scanner or by inputting the four digit code to register the bike for 90 minutes.
implicit_behaviors: (inferred) The biker can select one available bike from the list/area obtained in S5.
(inferred) The system must provide route guidance from the biker's location to the selected bike.
(inferred) Scanning the code or entering the four-digit code identifies the bike and creates a rental (registration) associated with the biker, with a start time.
(inferred) The project description states bikes are unlocked using a QR code, so registration is linked to unlocking the bike.
ambiguities: 'Scan the code on bike scanner' is unclear: whether the biker's device scans a code on the bike or the bike has a scanner that reads a code from the biker's device.
Whether the selected bike is reserved/held for the biker while navigating is not stated (another biker could register it first).
The rental period is fixed at 90 minutes here, which is inconsistent with S10 (specific minutes, a day, or a week).
Whether payment or a payment method is required before registration/unlocking is not stated.
How the bike is physically unlocked after registration is not described.

requirements.requirement_description: As soon as the bike is registered it must be removed from the list of available bikes.
implicit_behaviors: (inferred) The bike's availability status must change upon registration and be reflected in what all bikers see (S5) and in the administrator view (S12).
(inferred) Two bikers must not be able to register the same bike at the same time.
(inferred) A bike must return to the available list at the end of a rental, although the end of a rental is not specified.
ambiguities: 'As soon as' does not specify a maximum acceptable delay for the update.
The condition for a bike becoming available again (rental end/return) is not specified in any requirement.

requirements.requirement_description: The biker must be able to pay via their bank account or by their debit/credit card. Currently cash payments are not supported.
implicit_behaviors: (inferred) The system must interact with external payment capabilities; the project description requires compatibility with a variety of third-party payment platforms.
(inferred) Payment information must be protected according to the project description's security and privacy constraints.
(inferred) A payment record must be associated with a rental.
ambiguities: When payment occurs (before the ride, after the ride, pre-authorization, on overtime) is not stated.
Whether payment details are stored for reuse is not stated.
Which third-party payment platforms must be supported is not stated.
'Currently' suggests cash or other methods might be added in the future, but this is not explicit.

requirements.requirement_description: The app must notify the biker X minutes prior to the expiry of their rental time. Any overtime rides are subject to additional charges.
implicit_behaviors: (inferred) The system must track each active rental's expiry time and trigger a notification at a time before expiry.
(inferred) The system must detect overtime (rental continuing past expiry) and compute an additional charge, which links to payment (S8).
ambiguities: The value of 'X' is not specified, nor whether it is configurable or chosen by the biker.
The notification channel (in-app, push, SMS, email) is not stated.
The overtime charge rule (amount, granularity) is not stated.
How overtime ends is not stated because bike return is not specified.

requirements.requirement_description: The biker must be able to rent a bike for specific minutes, a day or for a week at maximum.
implicit_behaviors: (inferred) The biker must be able to choose a rental duration when renting.
(inferred) The rental duration determines the expiry time used by S9.
(inferred) Rentals longer than one week must not be allowed.
ambiguities: 'Specific minutes' is not defined (any number of minutes, predefined blocks, minimum duration).
Inconsistent with S6, which registers the bike for a fixed 90 minutes.
Whether pricing differs by rental type (minutes/day/week) is not stated.

requirements.requirement_description: The app allows the biker to view and download their bike usage history up to last 3 months in the form.
implicit_behaviors: (inferred) The system must keep a record of each biker's rentals for at least 3 months.
(inferred) The system must produce a downloadable representation of the history.
ambiguities: The sentence ends with 'in the form.' with no format given; the download format is unspecified.
Which data the history includes (dates, durations, locations/routes, charges) is not stated.
Whether data older than 3 months is deleted or only not shown to the biker is not stated (relevant to GDPR retention).

requirements.requirement_description: The bike administrator is able to view all of the bikes in the city as available or under utilization.
implicit_behaviors: (inferred) An administrator role distinct from the biker role exists and requires authenticated access.
(inferred) The system must provide the status (available / in use) of every bike in the city.
ambiguities: 'Under utilization' may mean 'currently in use' or 'under-utilized' (rarely used); the intended meaning is unclear.
Whether the view includes bike locations (map) is not stated.
Other bike states (e.g. maintenance, out of service) are not mentioned.
How administrators are registered/authenticated is not stated.

requirements.requirement_description: The administrator must be able to do an hourly and daily usage of the bikes.
implicit_behaviors: (inferred) The system must aggregate rental/usage data per hour and per day.
(inferred) This relies on the rental records also used by S11.
ambiguities: The verb is missing ('do an hourly and daily usage'): it is unclear whether the administrator views, generates, or exports a report, or something else.
The metrics to be included (number of rentals, utilization per bike, per area) are not stated.
Whether usage data shown to administrators is personal (per biker) or aggregated/anonymized is not stated (GDPR relevance).

cross_requirement_relationships.description: S2 states two different validity periods for the same verification code (30 minutes and 30 seconds).

S2: 'If the code is not entered within 30 seconds it is expired'

S7: 'As soon as the bike is registered it must be removed from the list of available bikes'

cross_requirement_relationships.description: Expiry notifications (S9) depend on the rental start established at registration (S6) and the rental duration (S6/S10).
evidence: S6: 'register the bike for 90 minutes'

S10: 'rent a bike for specific minutes, a day or for a week'
